content.thinking:
Let me analyze this OIML certificate markdown.

Certificate:
- number: R76/2006-DK3-17.15
- scheme: This is an OIML-CS certificate. Scheme A or B — the document doesn't explicitly say. R76/2006-DK3-17.15 — no scheme mentioned. I'll omit scheme since not present.
- member_state: Denmark
- date_issued: 1 December 2017
- oiml_issuer_id: DK3
- page_total: 2
- project_number: not present

Issuing authority:
- name: DELTA
- address_lines: ["Venlighedsvej 4", "2970 Hørsholm", "Denmark"]
- person_responsible: J. Hovgård Jensen
- person_title: Certification Manager
- phone: +45 7219 4000
- email: legal@delta.dk
- website: www.madebydelta.com
- oiml_issuer_id: DK3

Applicants:
- name: Tscale Electronics Mfg (Kunshan) Co., Ltd.
- address_lines: ["No.99 Shunchang Road", "Zhoushi, Kunshan, Jiangsu", "China"]

Manufacturers:
- Tscale Electronics Mfg (Kunshan) Co., Ltd. (no address given separately; same as applicant presumably)

Certified type:
- category: "Non-automatic weighing instrument" — hmm, category examples given are "Load cell", "Indicator", ... For NA WIs, maybe "Non-automatic weighing instrument". I'll use that.
- type_designations: ASP, ATP, AHP, AHPS, AHW, AHC, QSP, QTP, QHW, QHC, FX, FX-P
- module_designation: null
- description: "Non-automatic weighing instrument"

Recommendation:
- id: R76
- edition: 2006
- accuracy_classes: ["III", "IIII"]

Test reports:
- DANAK-1912801, dated 06-03-2013, 71 pages, role: test_report
- DANAK-1915746, dated 26-10-2015, 71 pages, test_report
- DANAK-1918487, dated 26-10-2017, 23 pages, test_report

Model family: 12 type designations, but no per-model characteristics table. The characteristics are given for the family as a whole (Max from 3 kg to 30 kg). Should I create model_family with models? The schema says include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant. There are 12 type designations. Hmm. The characteristics table doesn't vary per type — it gives ranges. I could include model_family with models listing the type designations. But the attributes don't vary. I think it's reasonable to include the models list with model_id for each type. Actually, rule 4 says detect matrix where attributes vary per model. Here nothing varies per model. The range "3 kg to 30 kg" is a type-level range, not per-model. I'll include model_family with models as the 12 type designations? Or skip model_family. Hmm.

The schema: `model_family:` include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant. The cert covers 12 types. So include model_family with models list. But no family_name. Actually maybe safer to just include type_designations in certified_type and skip model_family since no variant-specific data. But the schema says include only if >1 model variant — it does cover >1. I'll include it with model_ids being the type names, labels null? The models entries have model_id, label, attributes{}. I'll list them.

Hmm, but risk: could be seen as fabricating. It's not fabrication — the types are listed. I'll include.

Characteristics (type_level):
- accuracy_class: value "III and IIII" — hmm. Accuracy class III and IIII. That's a list of two classes. Type-level single value? Could be value: ["III", "IIII"]? The schema wants value as number|{min,max}|string. Could use string "III, IIII" or "III and IIII". I'll do value "III, IIII"? Actually recommendation.accuracy_classes covers it. I can skip accuracy_class in characteristics or include it. I'll include with value ["III","IIII"]? Not allowed shape. I'll use string "III and IIII". Hmm, maybe just omit since it's in recommendation. I'll include as type_level with value "III, IIII". Let me keep it simple: omit? The table has it. I'll include accuracy_class: {value: ["III", "IIII"], unit_symbol: null}? Strict shape says value: number | {min,max} | string. A list isn't allowed. I'll do string "III, IIII".

- weighing_range: value "Single-interval or multi-range or multi-interval" — string.
- maximum_capacity: Max_i, value {min: 3, max: 30}, unit_symbol "kg".
- minimum_capacity: Min_i, value "20 e_i" — formula/symbol, keep as string "20 ei". Value string "20 ei". Hmm, rule: formulas keep as string. "20 e_i" — I'll write "20 ei".
- verification_scale_interval: e_i ≥ 1 g → value {min: 1, max: null}, unit_symbol "g".
- number_of_intervals: Max/e: 3000 (single-interval), 2×3000 (multi-range), 2×3000 (multi-interval). This is a config-level thing? It varies by configuration (single-interval vs multi-range vs multi-interval). Could use config_level with axis "weighing_range_configuration". Values: {condition: "single-interval", value: 3000}, {condition: "multi-range", value: "2×3000"}, {condition: "multi-interval", value: "2×3000"}. Hmm, 2×3000 is a string. Could record as string "2x3000". I'll use config_level for this. Alternatively type_level string. Config level fits rule 5. Let me do config_level:
  {attribute: "number_of_intervals", axis: "weighing_range_configuration", values: [{condition: "single-interval", value: 3000, unit_symbol: null}, {condition: "multi-range", value: "2×3000", unit_symbol: null}, {condition: "multi-interval", value: "2×3000", unit_symbol: null}]}

  Note config_level values shape: {condition, value, unit_symbol}. OK.

- subtractive_tare: value "≤ -Max" → hmm. "≤ -Max" — string. unit null. I'll record subtractive_tare: {value: "-Max (up to)", ...}. Actually value string "≤ -Max" — but avoid LaTeX? ≤ is Unicode, fine. I'll use value {min: null, max: "-Max"}? Max is a symbol. Simpler: value "-Max", with maybe note. I'll do value: "-Max" and... hmm "≤ -Max". Keep string "≤ -Max".

- interface: value "Protective, according to paragraph 5.3.6" — string. Canonical label: interface.

- supply_voltage: "9-12 VDC / 230 VAC, 50 Hz using external AC/DC, 6V rechargeable battery (optional)". Split:
  - supply_voltage: multiple. There are two supply options: DC 9-12 V, AC 230 V, plus battery 6 V. 
    - supply_voltage_dc: {min: 9, max: 12}, unit "V"
    - supply_voltage_ac: 230, unit "V"
    - power_supply_frequency: 50, "Hz"
    - supply_voltage_battery: 6, "V" (optional)
  Label: supply_voltage_dc, supply_voltage_ac, power_supply_frequency, battery_voltage.
  
- temperature_range: -10 °C / +40 °C → {min: -10, max: 40}, unit "°C". Label: temperature_range_for_indicator or temperature_range. Canonical: temperature_range.

- software_identification: two values — legal relevant software: 1.11; application software: 01.xx. Could split: legal_relevant_software_version: "1.11", application_software_version: "01.xx".

Footnotes: none.

Revision history: none.

Matrix tables: none.

Components: none.

Date issued: "1 December 2017" → "2017-12-01".

Test report dates: 06-03-2013 → Danish format likely 6 March 2013 → "2013-03-06". 26-10-2015 → "2015-10-26". 26-10-2017 → "2017-10-26".

Test report role: "test reports" → test_report.

Cert number: R76/2006-DK3-17.15.

Scheme: not stated; R76/2006 certificates are scheme A typically but not stated — omit.

Let me also include type_level number_of_intervals? I'll use config_level for it. Or maybe keep in type_level as string. Config_level seems apt.

Certificate: page_total 2, member_state Denmark, date_issued "2017-12-01", oiml_issuer_id "DK3".

Final JSON.
